..Mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies this afternoon 
across southeast Arizona with surface dewpoints in the 50s and 
precipitable water values ranging from about 0.7 to 1 inch across 
the region. There is just enough moisture for some cloud build-ups 
this afternoon and isolated showers and thunderstorms mainly from 
southern Pinal county extending southward through the Tucson Metro 
and down through Santa Cruz County to the Int'l border. These storms 
don't look particularly impactful but some gusty winds up to 40 mph 
can occur with storm activity today. These storms will tend to 
diminish after sunset this evening. 

This weekend is looking particularly active as troughing off the 
California coast results in recurvature of Tropical Storm Rachel 
today with rapid movement to the northeast and expected landfall as 
a Tropical Storm across far northern Baja late Saturday night or 
early Sunday morning. The impacts from this system are now pretty 
well baked in across our area for the weekend. On Saturday, 
increased moisture will help result in scattered showers and 
thunderstorms especially Saturday afternoon and evening. A few of 
these storms could be strong to locally severe with wind gusts of 40 
to 60 mph and produce locally heavy rain along with small hail. The 
greatest uncertainty for Saturday remains how unstable the airmass 
becomes which will determine the intensity of the thunderstorms. Any 
stronger thunderstorms that develop could drop a quick half inch to 
inch of rain or so with an isolated flash flood threat. Meanwhile, 
as Rachel skirts by to our west, there is a non-zero tornado threat 
as early as Saturday afternoon but especially Saturday night into 
early Sunday mainly across western Pima County as shear and helicity 
parameters are more favorable for these locales. The SPC has placed 
locales from Tucson westward in a marginal risk severe thunderstorms 
for Day 2 (12Z Sat to 12Z Sun) with a 2% tornado risk for western 
Pima County.

The combination of Rachel swinging through to our west Saturday 
night and the troughing aloft will result in breezy to windy 
conditions for most of southeast Arizona on Sunday. Expect south to 
southwest winds of 25 to 35 mph from Tucson westward and gusts of 45 
to 55 mph with winds a bit lower east of Tucson. Any convective 
activity will also result in the potential for stronger winds being 
mixed down. Wind Advisories have been hoisted from Tucson westward 
on Sunday. As Rachel swings north, our area will remain in southerly 
flow with scattered thunderstorms once again on Sunday. Total rain 
amounts this weekend will generally be in the 0.25" to 0.75" range 
from Tucson westward and 0.10" to 0.25" range east of Tucson with up 
to 1 to 2 inches in the mountains and within locales that happen to 
see a couple of rounds of stronger thunderstorms. It should be noted 
that precipitation for this event will be more variable and while 
these are areal averages, some locales could conceivably end up with 
little rainfall when all is said and done. 

Southerly flow continues on Monday ahead of the longwave trough with 
breezy winds continuing. While moisture levels back off on Monday 
(PWAT 0.75" to 1 inch), the combination of this moisture and 
increased lift and forcing ahead of the trough will result in 
isolated to low end scattered showers and thunderstorms. Certainly 
not looking as widespread as the weekend but rain chances continue 
nonetheless. We'll still have the upper low to our north on Tuesday 
as well for potential for a few lingering showers. By Wednesday, 
drying has moved back into our area and with dry conditions through 
the remainder of the work week. 

Temperatures will drop to near normal temperatures on Saturday, then 
an extended period of below normal temperatures will occur Sunday 
through the middle of next week.
